summary: Top AI executives and experts, including OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, signed a statement warning that AI poses a risk of extinction comparable to pandemics and nuclear war, urging policymakers to prioritize mitigation. The statement was published by the Center for AI Safety and included CEOs from DeepMind and Anthropic, as well as AI pioneers Geoffrey Hinton and Yoshua Bengio. The letter coincided with U.S.-EU discussions on AI regulation.

claims.text: More than 350 signatories, including top AI executives and experts, signed a statement warning that AI poses a risk of extinction comparable to pandemics and nuclear war.
claims.evidence_quote: Mitigating the risk of extinction from AI should be a global priority alongside other societal-scale risks such as pandemics and nuclear war," more than 350 signatories wrote in a letter

claims.text: The statement was published by the nonprofit Center for AI Safety (CAIS).
claims.evidence_quote: published by the nonprofit Center for AI Safety (CAIS).

claims.text: Signatories included CEOs of AI firms DeepMind and Anthropic, and executives from Microsoft and Google.
claims.evidence_quote: they included the CEOs of AI firms DeepMind and Anthropic, and executives from Microsoft and Google.

claims.text: Geoffrey Hinton and Yoshua Bengio, two of the three 'godfathers of AI' who received the 2018 Turing Award, were among the signatories.
claims.evidence_quote: Also among them were Geoffrey Hinton and Yoshua Bengio - two of the three so-called "godfathers of AI" who received the 2018 Turing Award for their work on deep learning

claims.text: The statement singled out Meta, where the third godfather of AI, Yann LeCun, works, for not signing the letter.
claims.evidence_quote: A statement from CAIS singled out Meta, where the third godfather of AI, Yann LeCun, works, for not signing the letter.

claims.text: The letter coincided with the U.S.-EU Trade and Technology Council meeting in Sweden where politicians were expected to talk about regulating AI.
claims.evidence_quote: The letter coincided with the U.S.-EU Trade and Technology Council meeting in Sweden where politicians are expected to talk about regulating AI.

claims.text: Elon Musk and a group of AI experts and industry executives were the first to cite potential risks to society in April.
claims.evidence_quote: Elon Musk and a group of AI experts and industry executives were the first ones to cite potential risks to society in April.

claims.text: AI pioneer Hinton earlier told Reuters that AI could pose a 'more urgent' threat to humanity than climate change.
claims.evidence_quote: AI pioneer Hinton earlier told Reuters that AI could pose a "more urgent" threat to humanity than climate change.

claims.text: Last week OpenAI CEO Sam Altman referred to EU AI regulation as over-regulation and threatened to leave Europe, but reversed his stance within days after criticism.
claims.evidence_quote: Last week OpenAI CEO Sam Altman referred to EU AI - the first efforts to create a regulation for AI - as over-regulation and threatened to leave Europe. He reversed his stance within days after criticism from politicians.

claims.text: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen was scheduled to meet Altman on Thursday.
claims.evidence_quote: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will meet Altman on Thursday.
